summary: Karl Hoffmann specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Ferdinand Sommer and Walther Wüst, and held chairs at Saarland University (1952–1955) and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (1955–1983).

Karl Jettmar was an archaeologist and historian who earned his doctorate from the University of Vienna. He held positions at the University of Vienna, Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, and served as director at Heidelberg University (1964–1986).

Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz and the University of Würzburg. He taught at Kronberg-Gymnasium Aschaffenburg before becoming a professor at the University of Bonn in 1818.

Karl Lachmann worked in linguistics and related fields. After studying at Leipzig University and the University of Göttingen, he held a long-term academic post at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1825 to 1851.
Karl Marbe worked in linguistics after studying at the University of Bonn. He held academic posts at the University of Würzburg (circa 1896–1935) and Goethe University Frankfurt (circa 1905–1909).

Karl Otfried Müller was a historian, archaeologist, and linguist. He studied at the universities of Breslau and Berlin under August Boeckh, Friedrich Schleiermacher, and Friedrich August Wolf, and became a professor at the University of Göttingen in 1819.

Karl Popper was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Cambridge. He held academic positions at the University of Canterbury, the London School of Economics, and the University of London (1949–1969).

Karl Richard Lepsius was a historian, archaeologist, and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Berlin. He held a chair at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1846–1884) and served as Chief Librarian at Berlin State Library.

Karl Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied under G. W. F. Hegel in Berlin and at Halle and Heidelberg. He held an extraordinariat at Halle before taking a chair at the University of Königsberg in 1833.

Karl Verner worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at the University of Copenhagen and under August Leskien. He worked as a librarian at Halle (~1876–1883) and became a docent in Slavic studies at Copenhagen in 1882.

Karl-Heinz Brodbeck is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Munich. He held posts at the University of Munich and was a professor at Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt (1992–2014).

Karl-Heinz Everding is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD at the University of Bonn and his habilitation at the University of Hamburg. He served as Privatdozent at Hamburg in 1999 and joined the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Karl-Heinz Gottmann was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Anagarika Govinda from circa 1952 to 1985, succeeding him in 1982.
Karma Drubgyü Ngedön Nyingpo studied under Pema Wangchok Gyelpo and Khakyab Dorje.
Karma Lek Shé Drayang was a scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Karma Lekshe Tsomo is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. She served as a professor at the University of San Diego and held a professorship at Hawaiʻi in 2023.
Karma Lodrö Chökyi Sengge worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued traditional studies under Kalu Rinpoche in 1973 and under Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje.

Karma Phuntsho is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his D.Phil. at Oxford under Michael Aris and Richard Gombrich, and later held research and fellowship positions at the University of Cambridge and CNRS.
Karma Shedrub Chokyi Sengge studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Pema Wangchok Gyelpo, and taught Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Karma Sonam Palmo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned degrees at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed a PhD at the University of Tasmania under Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.
